## TL;DR

Added `just deploy-phone` — a Bun TypeScript port of the Laisen/Tiao Tailscale adb deploy flow for RepoOS Hub. Debug builds use `applicationIdSuffix ".dev"` (`org.repoos.mobile.dev`) so they install beside release. Phone targets come from env or `~/.config/repoos-hub/phone` with no default IP in the repo. Vitest covers connect, scan fallback, launch-component validation, signature mismatch, and `--no-build` / `--no-scan`. No real install was run; Nick should approve the first live deploy.

## Work and rationale

I read the Laisen reference on the thinkpad (`deploy-phone.sh`, `launch-component.sh`, `phone-deploy.md`) and the Tiao copy for env naming, then matched Laisen's connection behaviour while respecting Hub privacy constraints.

Target resolution order: `REPOOS_HUB_PHONE` (full `ip:port`), then `REPOOS_HUB_PHONE_PORT` combined with the IP from the saved config file, then `~/.config/repoos-hub/phone`. Unlike Laisen, there is no baked-in default Tailscale IP in the repository; if nothing is configured the script exits with a clear setup message rather than guessing an address.

Connection order: try the saved `ip:port`; if that fails, probe other wireless adb serials already listed by `adb devices` for the same IP; if scanning is allowed, scan TCP ports 30000–49999 using `nmap` when available, otherwise concurrent socket connect probes. After each `adb connect`, the script waits one second before requiring `adb get-state` to return `device`, then persists the last working address back to the config file.

The deploy path builds via `just build-android` (keeps Capacitor web sync aligned), installs the debug APK with `adb install -r -d`, force-stops the package, launches via `am start -n` using a fully qualified component, and prints the short git commit. `INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE` triggers one-time guidance to `adb uninstall org.repoos.mobile.dev` and stops.

Implementation is split into `scripts/lib/launch-component.ts`, `scripts/lib/hub-phone-deploy.ts` (testable core with injectable adb runner, sleep, and port scan), and `scripts/deploy-phone.ts` (CLI). The justfile mobile group exposes `deploy-phone *FLAGS` → `bun scripts/deploy-phone.ts`.

## Approaches tried

Bash parity was the behavioural spec; TypeScript + dependency injection was chosen for tests because AGENTS.md requires Bun scripts and the vitest gate already lives under `src/ui-app/tests/`.

Gradle `debug { applicationIdSuffix ".dev" }` mirrors Laisen side-by-side dev installs. Release `applicationId` remains `org.repoos.mobile`. Debug `app/src/debug/res/values/strings.xml` sets launcher label **RepoOS Hub Dev** without touching release strings. Launch uses `org.repoos.mobile.dev/org.repoos.mobile.MainActivity` — never a relative `.MainActivity`, which would resolve against the suffixed application id.

Documentation lives in `docs/phone-deploy.md` plus a short pointer in `mobile/README.md`, covering adb install, JDK/SDK expectations, Tailscale naming, fixed port 5555 vs Wireless debugging, the Tailscale warning-triangle toggle, and the single-session Wireless debugging limit.

## Challenges and blockers

Port-scan tests required careful fake-adb sequencing: the saved port must fail connect while a scanned port succeeds only after connect, without marking the stale port as ready. The unreachable-phone test aligned temporary `homeDir` and `repoRoot` paths so failure text matched `phoneConfigPath(homeDir)`.

Human verification remains out of scope: this task deliberately does not run `adb install` against Nick's phone. The first real `just deploy-phone` will install **org.repoos.mobile.dev** next to any existing **org.repoos.mobile** release build (or replace an older dev build with the same id).

## Key learnings

Hub deploy reuses Laisen's Tailscale + Wireless debugging ergonomics with stricter privacy: configuration lives only on the machine (`REPOOS_HUB_*` and `~/.config/repoos-hub/phone`). APK outputs and Gradle caches are gitignored under `mobile/android/.gitignore` and `mobile/.gitignore`.
